intended_object: The map (c, x) ↦ c • x from ℝ × ℝ³ to ℝ³, written as a bilinear map. It is used as the bilinear pairing in a Mathlib convolution, so that a scalar mollifier can be convolved with vector-valued initial data (inferred from the docstring and from its use on line 60, where it is turned into a continuous bilinear map with mkContinuous₂).
explanation: The body is just scalar multiplication on L2Vec3 = PiLp 2 (Fin 3 → ℝ), packaged as an ℝ-bilinear map with LinearMap.mk₂. The four proof obligations are add_smul, mul_smul, smul_add and smul_comm, and they are all correct. Its only role is to supply the bilinear map that Mathlib's convolution API needs (via mkContinuous₂), which makes it an implementation device rather than a mathematical notion in its own right. Mathlib already provides the same map in general: LinearMap.lsmul ℝ L2Vec3 for the linear version and ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul for the continuous one. So the definition re-implements an existing Mathlib map in one particular setting, but it is correct.
